definition: Whether a model's weights are downloadable and self-hostable (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral) or accessible only through an API (Claude, GPT, Gemini).
details: Whether a model's weights are downloadable and self-hostable (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral) or accessible only through an API (Claude, GPT, Gemini). "Open weights" is not the same as open source: training data and code often remain closed, and licenses may restrict use.

explainer.lead: This is the distinction between models whose weights are downloadable and self-hostable (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral) and those accessible only through an API (Claude, GPT, Gemini). It matters because it determines whether you can run and modify a model yourself or must rely on a provider.

tiers.eli5: Some AI models you can download and keep; others you can only talk to over the internet through someone else's service.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers choose open weights when they need self-hosting and customization, and closed APIs when they want provider-managed access. Pitfall: "open weights" is not the same as open source, since training data and code often remain closed and licenses may restrict use.
tiers.paperLevel: A categorization: open-weights models have downloadable, self-hostable weights; closed models are accessible only through an API. Open weights does not imply open source.

explainer.example: A team needing on-premises deployment picks a self-hostable Llama model, while another content with hosted access uses a closed API model.
